name: gizza-ai/srt-to-plaintext
summary: Strip SRT/WebVTT cue numbers and timestamps into plain transcript text.

tool.description: Convert SubRip (.srt) or WebVTT subtitle text into a plain transcript. It removes cue numbers, timestamp ranges and blank separators, then returns only caption text. Options choose one line per cue, preserved cue blocks or one paragraph; strip formatting tags; remove bracketed sound-effect/music cues; remove leading speaker labels; and collapse consecutive duplicate captions. The parser is deterministic and local: it never executes anything and accepts common SRT/WebVTT timing lines with comma or dot milliseconds.

dedupe.description: Collapse consecutive duplicate captions, useful for rolling auto-caption exports. Comparison is case-insensitive. Default false.

input.description: SubRip (.srt) or WebVTT subtitle text. Cue numbers, timing lines like 00:00:01,000 --> 00:00:04,000, and blank separators are removed; only caption text is returned.

layout.description: Output layout: lines = one cleaned caption per line (default), blocks = preserve cue line breaks with blank lines between cues, paragraph = one flowing paragraph.

remove_sound_effects.description: Remove bracketed non-speech cues such as [applause] or (door slams), plus musical-note markers. Default false.

remove_speaker_labels.description: Remove leading speaker labels such as NARRATOR: or - JOHN:. Heuristic and off by default to avoid clipping genuine dialogue.

strip_tags.description: Remove inline formatting tags such as <i>, <b>, <font ...>, and ASS/SSA override blocks like {\an8}. Default true.
